set.body:
WHY: graph4s Graph rejects self-loops (ConnectError.SelfLoop) and cannot hold parallel edges; consumers with labelled multi-relations (two roles between the same pair, reflexive relations) currently have no sanctioned path.

SCOPE: with the neighbourhood protocol, multigraphs are representable natively by adapters. This bead documents and tests the policy: (a) parallel keyed incidences are first-class and refine as a multiset; (b) self-loops are first-class incidences with other == v and are counted once per orientation; (c) the graph4s adapter keeps graph4s's simple-graph rules and reports a typed error for unsupported inputs rather than silently dropping edges; (d) a helper `Reify.relationsAsVertices` in grakern-standard (topology-neutral) turns labelled edges into keyed vertices for consumers who need edge attributes to participate in node refinement.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
1. Multiset semantics: two parallel incidences with equal keys yield a different colour than one incidence (count matters) and the same colour regardless of enumeration order.
2. Self-loop semantics documented and tested; undirected self-loop contributes one neighbour entry.
3. graph4s adapter: attempting to build from a graph4s input with an unsupported feature returns Left(typed error), never a partial sample.
4. Reify helper: for any labelled graph, reify then WL equals a documented reference construction; reification is deterministic and alpha-invariant.

PROPOSED TESTS
- MultiEdgeSuite: parallel vs single; order shuffle invariance.
- SelfLoopSuite: loop vs no loop differ; loop counted once.
- Graph4sAdapterErrorSuite: typed error on unsupported input.
- ReifySuite: property — reify(alpha(g)) == alpha(reify(g)); reify is injective on labelled-edge multisets.
